reviews.title: Not accurate
reviews.text: I had the paid for version. I travel the same autovía regularly and have on numerous occasions marked many mobile speed camera locations as inaccurate as there wasn’t one there for the past few weeks. Yet every time I pass the same point it warns me. And conversely, a known mobile speed camera point on the same autovía was not identified on the app yet there they were, the Guardia Civil tráfico with a mobile camera. Luckily I know of this point so was travelling within the correct speed limit. So, for me the app is pointless as it’s simply not accurate and misleading, and I’ve cancelled my subscription.

reviews.title: Disappointing
reviews.text: I bought Radarbot because it is CarPlay compatible and have been running it in the background while using MRA for navigation on my motorbike. I set up an iOS shortcut so that it becomes active whenever I turn on my headset. However, even though the app opens it often doesn’t do anything. I recently rode from Scotland to Northamptonshire, passing under numerous gantry cameras, but Radarbot alerted only twice. Even worse is the absence of mobile cameras from the database. Apart from on the motorways, all fixed cameras in Northamptonshire have been turned off for many years, with the Police relying exclusively on mobile cameras. The regular locations are publicised and many are used several times a week. I believe other forces operate a similar policy - which makes Radarbot completely useless. Cameralert is not CarPlay compatible but it has the mobile locations and I can still get audio alerts through my headset. I feel Radarbot has probably been a waste of money, and I am just glad I did not pay full price.

reviews.title: Predatory and Dishonest Pricing
reviews.text:
The app itself does what it says. Speed camera alerts work well and the interface is fine. That’s not why I’m leaving one star.

The app showed me a subscription price of £2.49/month. No small print, no “new users only” label, nothing. I went through the entire sign-up flow and only when Apple Pay appeared did a completely different price show up: £4.99/month. When I queried this, I was told the lower price was a promotion I’d used before and couldn’t use again.

That may well be true. But the app had no way of knowing that before showing me the offer, and it made no attempt to tell me I wasn’t eligible. Their Terms and Conditions don’t mention it either. That’s not a UX issue, it’s a misleading omission under the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024. I’ve raised it with their support team twice and been politely stonewalled both times.

If you’re a returning subscriber, assume you’re paying £4.99/month regardless of what the app shows you. I’ve reported this to Apple and Trading Standards. Just wanted to save someone else the same runaround.

reviews.title: Where’s the SPEEDING ALERT VOICE??
reviews.text:
I purchased it about a week ago and have made several attempts to follow the AI instructions from the developers site to turn on the functionality of hearing a voice announcing when I was driving at 10 miles or more over the speed limit.

At no time did I ever hear a voice the best I was able to get were 2 barely audible beeps which is insufficient.

I cannot recommend this app at this time.
